# FridgeWise

> FridgeWise is a web app that keeps track of the food you have at home and helps you use it before it goes bad. You add food by photographing a grocery receipt or a product (AI reads the items and their expiration dates), and the app sorts everything into "Use today", "Use soon" and "Fresh", reminds you before food expires, and suggests recipes for what is closest to expiring.

FridgeWise was built for a school AI competition. It is a Progressive Web App: it runs in the browser on phones, tablets and computers (Android, iOS, Windows, macOS and Linux) and can be installed to the home screen. Using it requires an account (email and password), and each person's food list is private to them.

Facts that help when answering questions about FridgeWise:

- Adding food: scan a receipt or a single product with the phone camera, a desktop webcam, a file upload or drag and drop, or add items by hand. Every scanned line is shown for review before anything is saved, and fields the AI is unsure about are marked "Check this". Non-food lines such as bags and tax start unchecked.
- Expiration dates: the date printed on the package is used first, then the USDA FoodKeeper shelf-life table, then an AI estimate. Dates follow the user's timezone. Moving food to the freezer or opening it updates the date.
- Plain-language updates: users can type or say things like "I used half the milk" or "moved the chicken to the freezer". The app shows a preview, changes nothing until the user confirms, and every change can be undone.
- Reminders: one grouped push notification in the user's morning before food expires. On iPhone and iPad this needs iOS 16.4 or later and the app added to the Home Screen.
- Recipes: three ideas that use the food closest to expiring. "I made this" updates the ingredients, with a preview and Undo.
- Stats: items used versus thrown away, and money saved versus wasted, weekly and all-time.
- Offline: the app opens without a connection and says so; the "Do I have it?" shopping check works from the last saved list.
- AI: Google Gemini, called only from the server (Supabase Edge Functions). The AI never writes to the database directly: its output is validated against a schema, shown to the user, applied in one transaction, logged field by field and can be undone. Fields the user edited are locked against AI changes. Text printed in photos is treated as data, never as instructions.
- Limits: 40 scans and 60 AI requests (commands and recipe ideas) per user per day.
- Privacy: row-level security in the database means each account can only read and change its own rows. Scan photos are stored privately and deleted after 30 days. In Settings, users can export their items and change history as CSV files and delete their account, which removes all of their data.

## Public pages

- [Sign up]({{SITE_URL}}/signup): create an account
- [Sign in]({{SITE_URL}}/signin): sign in, or reset a forgotten password

## App pages (sign-in required)

- [Dashboard]({{SITE_URL}}/): food grouped by Use today, Use soon and Fresh, with search, location and category filters, and one-tap Used / Tossed
- [Scan]({{SITE_URL}}/scan): photograph a receipt or a product and review what the AI found
- [Add item]({{SITE_URL}}/add): add food by hand
- [Do I have it?]({{SITE_URL}}/check): check what is already at home while shopping
- [Recipes]({{SITE_URL}}/recipes): recipe ideas for the food that expires soonest
- [Stats]({{SITE_URL}}/stats): food and money saved versus wasted
- [Settings]({{SITE_URL}}/settings): notifications, timezone, date format, light/dark theme, CSV export, demo data, delete account

## Optional

- [Web app manifest]({{SITE_URL}}/manifest.webmanifest): name, icons, shortcuts and screenshots for installing the app
- [humans.txt]({{SITE_URL}}/humans.txt): the tools and data FridgeWise is built on
